title: Commit attribution
summary: Git hooks and account keys that keep AI and bot identities out of your commit history.
why: This is the mechanism behind the attribution floor: the floor states the rule, these items enforce it at the harness, at commit time and before any push.

items.title: commit-msg hook strips AI trailers
items.does: Records your identity in local git config, copies kit_identity.py and adds a commit-msg check (run by the git hook dispatchers of the ci-gates module) that removes forbidden attribution lines.
items.why: This is the prevention step: the trailer is removed before the commit exists, so nothing has to be rewritten later.

items.title: pre-push hook refuses foreign identities
items.does: Adds a pre-push check that refuses a push whose new commits carry a non-owner author, committer or attribution trailer.
items.why: It is the last check before the code host records a contributor; a mistake caught here never becomes public history.

items.title: No attribution footer from Claude
items.does: Sets the account keys attribution.commit and attribution.pr to empty and includeCoAuthoredBy to false.
items.why: Stopping the trailer at its source means the hooks rarely have anything to strip.

items.title: History rewrite helper
items.does: Copies kit_rewrite.py, which plans, bundles and then rewrites foreign identities out of history, only when you run it with the plan's confirmation id.
items.why: History that is already polluted can be cleaned, but a rewrite must never happen implicitly; the helper makes a backup bundle first and needs your explicit go.
items.notes: Never runs on its own. The UI shows the plan only; running it needs your typed confirmation.
